Marcus/Team/Sarah —

Drafting language below for use in the Redwood Console and for procurement docs. Kept each line intentionally short and neutral. Please flag if any edits needed.

1) Residency (console blurb, single sentence):
"Hosted customers may select regional data residency where available; when EU residency is requested we confine customer-associated hosted data to the selected EU region and apply standard technical and contractual safeguards."

2) Subprocessors (console blurb, single sentence):
"Redwood maintains a current list of subprocessors and will provide advance notice for material changes; the list is available in the Console and in the DPA."

3) Audit logs (procurement answer):
"Redwood retains operational audit logs for infrastructure and access events for a baseline of 90 days; for customers requiring longer retention we offer contractable retention terms as part of Dedicated/Private deployments or via an add-on for hosted customers."

Notes/assumptions:
- "Select regional data residency where available" reflects that residency depends on region availability in the customer's contract/plan.
- For truly regulated EU-only requirements we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment (we can include a sentence noting that).

I can also produce a 1-paragraph plain-English summary for a procurement one-pager if helpful.

Kimberly Park
Senior Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference

- For the subprocessor line, procurement asked if the console link is public or behind login — they prefer copy that clarifies "available to customers in the Console (authenticated)".
- Audit logs: procurement will accept the 90-day baseline if we explicitly call out that extension requires contract amendment or an add-on.

If you can send the two one-liners updated with those three micro-edits, we can close this in procurement and push the integration into our vendor registry.
